# Specification Quality Checklist: Automatic Legacy Tamil Encoding Detection

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2026-11-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirements Quality

- [x] CHK001 User stories are prioritized by importance: P1 (MVP detection across 7 encodings), P2 (ambiguity & uncertainty handling), P3 (multi-runtime bindings).
- [x] CHK002 Acceptance scenarios include concrete input types (raw byte arrays, 16-bit CID vectors, UTF-8 strings).
- [x] CHK003 Edge cases explicitly define behavior for native UTF-8 Tamil text, mixed language streams, and short/empty inputs.
- [x] CHK004 Detection thresholds and scoring metrics are quantitatively defined (e.g. confidence >= 0.60, delta >= 0.15).
- [x] CHK005 Functional requirements cover Rust engine scoring, unified dispatcher exposure, and tri-runtime wrappers.
- [x] CHK006 Measurable success criteria establish clear accuracy (> 98%), latency (< 5 μs), and test corpus requirements.

## Notes

- Trie structures in `crates/tamil-codec` already contain complete edge maps for all 7 encodings, allowing scoring to reuse existing trie tables without large auxiliary data.
- Multi-runtime exposure can follow standard dispatcher routing pattern.
